 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. The  Charlotte Hornets  faced a difficult situation in 2023 involving  Miles Bridges . The forward was charged with domestic violence, and right around the same time, his contract was up. 
 Outgoing majority owner  Michael Jordan  and the rest of the Hornets front office should have already decided whether to re-sign Bridges. Despite the controversy, Hornets general manager Mitch Kupchak revealed that Jordan, along with incoming owners Gabe Plotkin and Rick Schnall, unanimously agreed to keep the forward.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Given the seriousness of the allegations and the public scrutiny surrounding the case, Kupchak acknowledged that evaluating Bridges' remorse and accountability was not easy. In the end, Jordan and the Hornets management decided to give him another chance.
 "You have to make a judgment, right?"  Kupchak  said  at the time.  "Is this sincere remorse? Is this sincere accountability? It is not something that is easy to judge. We took all of those factors into consideration and ultimately gave him a second chance." 
 Hornets knew not everybody was pleased with their decision on Bridges 
 Bridges had missed the entire 2022-23 season after being arrested in June 2022 following an incident involving the mother of his children. He pleaded no contest in November 2022 to a felony domestic violence charge in Los Angeles County. 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Bridges then received three years of probation and was ordered to complete 52 weeks of domestic violence counseling, alongside other court-imposed conditions. For its part, the NBA subsequently suspended him for 30 games following its investigation.
 However, the league credited Bridges with 20 games for the time he had already missed. This change meant he served 10 additional games at the beginning of the 2022-23 season. Miles' situation affected the Hornets as he was one of the team's most productive players. In the 2021-22 season, he averaged 20.2 points, 7.0 rebounds and 3.8 assists per game.
 For the Hornets, the best course of action was to re-sign Bridges. At the same time, Kupchak recognized that the Hornets' decision would not satisfy everyone, particularly those who are opposed to domestic violence.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "Obviously it is a polarizing topic,"  Kupchak admitted.  "Everybody may not agree. It's a tough situation to be in." 
 To prevent potential backlash, Kupchak made clear that Bridges' return to the Hornets did not automatically restore the trust he had lost.
 "[Bridges] He understands that even though his teammates are happy to have him back, there is some trust that needs to be earned back,"  he added.
 Related: "He's been pretty much a jerk almost his entire life" – Nuggets coach slammed Kareem Abdul-Jabbar before his final All-Star Game 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Bridges swore to become a better person and family man 
 Bridges returned to the Hornets knowing that his actions would continue to shape how the management and fans viewed him. He acknowledged that not everyone believed he deserved another opportunity, but swore to rebuild his reputation.
 "Yes, I understand that some people don't think I deserve a second chance,"  he said.  "That's why I am trying to use this year to prove to everybody the person that I am. Who is Miles Bridges? It's not what people think he is." 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Bridges also took the opportunity to apologize to his family and to everyone involved for the inconvenience he had caused.
 "I want to apologize to everybody for the pain and embarrassment that I have caused everyone, especially my family,"  he stated.  "This year away I've used to prioritize going to therapy and becoming the best person I can be — someone that my family and everyone here can be proud of." 
 Bridges redeemed himself before being traded by the Hornets 
 Bridges bounced back and proved he deserved the one-year, $7.9 million deal he signed that year. In 69 games, he averaged 21.0 points and 7.3 rebounds per game.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Bridges' impressive comeback year resulted in another and bigger contract extension. In 2024, the Hornets re-signed him to a three-year, $75 million contract.
 Bridges went on to produce remarkable numbers for the Hornets. However, this past summer, Miles was traded to the Phoenix Suns.
